title: How to Convert a Finance Analyst Salary from Hourly to Annual Using a 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how to convert a finance analyst salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week, 52-week year, and the fortnight. Includes National Minimum Wage, casual loading, super, an
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is the hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 (38 × 52).

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary using a 38-hour week?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 (hours per week) and then by 52 (weeks per year). For example, $30 per hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. The fortnightly equivalent is your weekly pay multiplied by 2.

faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026?
faqs.a: From the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% on the same date. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and published by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

faqs.q: How does casual loading and superannuation affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading (usually 25%) is paid on top of the base hourly rate and is not included in the base rate. Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 2026–27), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your base hourly rate is $26.44, your casual rate is $33.05, and your employer also contributes an additional 12% super on your ordinary earnings.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the 38-hour week and the 52-week year

When you are offered a **finance analyst salary** or any hourly rate, the standard way to compare it to an annual figure is to multiply by the hours you work each week and then by 52 weeks. In Australia, full-time work is commonly based on a 38-hour week under many awards and the National Employment Standards. This means the annual gross pay formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

That is 1,976 hours per year. For example, if your hourly rate is $40, your annual salary would be $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040. This straightforward calculation lets you quickly assess a **finance analyst salary** offer or compare job advertisements that list hourly rates.

## From hourly to annual: the formula in practice

To apply the formula, simply take your base hourly rate (before any casual loading or penalties) and multiply by 38, then by 52. The result is your gross annual pay before tax and before super. If you are paid fortnightly, your gross fortnightly pay is your hourly rate × 76 (38 × 2). This can help you budget across pay cycles.

It is important to note that this calculation assumes you work exactly 38 hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. If your role includes regular overtime or shift penalties, your actual annual earnings will be higher. For a more precise estimate tailored to your award, use the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman or the Pay and Conditions Tool.

## The National Minimum Wage and award rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission and published by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% on the same date. Many employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their classification. For example, a **finance analyst salary** under the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award may have specific pay rates above the national minimum. Always check the relevant award pay guide to confirm your minimum entitlement.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. So a casual worker on the National Minimum Wage earns $33.05 per hour. This loading is paid in lieu of paid leave entitlements. When converting a casual hourly rate to annual, use the base rate (without loading) for the formula, then add the loading separately. For more detail, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

## Superannuation is paid on top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings (from 2026–27) on top of your gross pay. This means the total cost to your employer is higher than your annual salary. The super guarantee is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your hourly rate; it is an additional payment into your super fund. For more information, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and take-home pay

Your take-home pay depends on your annual gross income and the tax withheld. For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). The Australian Taxation Office provides a gross pay estimator to help you estimate your gross pay from net pay, or you can use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide. Remember that this is an estimate only; your actual tax may vary if you have deductions, offsets, or a HELP debt.

## Finance analyst salary in context

When evaluating a **finance analyst salary**, the hourly rate is often the starting point for negotiation. Using the 38-hour week conversion, a **finance analyst salary** offer of $80,000 per year equates to approximately $40.49 per hour. Conversely, if you are offered an hourly rate of $45, your annual equivalent would be $88,920. This quick conversion helps you compare roles across industries and employment types.

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which corresponds to an annual salary of about $108,352.40 (based on 52 weeks). For all employees (including part-time), average total earnings were $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118.40 per year. These figures provide a benchmark for a **finance analyst salary**, though actual pay depends on experience, location, and the specific employer.

## Summary of key assumptions

- **Hours per week:** 38 (full-time standard)
- **Weeks per year:** 52
- **Annual gross formula:** hourly rate × 38 × 52
- **Fortnightly gross:** hourly rate × 76
- **Super:** 12% paid on top of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base
- **Tax:** 2026–27 resident rates plus Medicare levy

Always refer to the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for the latest rates and the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for benchmarks. For a personalised calculation, use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and add casual loading if applicable.
